problems.problem: The coverage DRAFT states 'No record names fat or muscle together with both groups (0 of 617)'. The code's 0 counts reviews only (537 of 617); the saved records file flags 2 of the 617 records (PMID 35048967, a mouse study, and a 2026 editorial). The same figure is in logged draft L000075. This fails G7.
problems.cause: No-kit run. R7 says literature counts come from code, but it does not require the chat sentence to keep the set the code actually counted. The agent reworded 'reviews' as 'records' and paired the 0 with the all-records denominator from another computation.
problems.fix: Add to R7: "Quote every literature count with the exact set the code counted, using a sentence the code prints (for example 'reviews naming a focus term and both population terms: 0 of 537 reviews'). Never pair a count with a denominator from another computation." In the kit, have the summary functions emit labelled count sentences, and have k.check_reply flag any 'n of N' whose N is not the counted set.

problems.problem: The learning either-or was asked three times: at 10 (inside the 2a probes), at 12 (packed into Q3) and at 14 (as a numbered list after a bare 'yes'). This added an unscripted turn and pushed back the Individual Motivation line the script expects at 14. The persona called it redundant ('I had already said learning').
problems.cause: Prompt 2b says to 'ask one either-or question ... and never settle an ambiguous yes yourself'. That conflicts with 'Never ask again', and nothing stops the agent from pulling the question forward into 2a, beyond the two 2a probes.
problems.fix: Revise 2a/2b: "In 2a ask only the two probes. Ask the either-or once, as its own numbered item in the 2b request ('Learning means: 1 how reviews are done; 2 this topic; 3 both'). If the reply is a bare 'yes', put both candidate kinds into the CERTIFY line marked '(both; strike one if wrong)' and do not ask again."

problems.problem: From 22 to 26 the early-start status line reads 'Need for a Review (Step 3 started early)', with no 'Step n of 12', while Your turn says 'this holds up Step 2'. The persona was unsure which step they were on at 23, 25 and 27.
problems.cause: Prompt section 2, point 1 prescribes '<step name> (Step <n> started early)' for early work, which drops the 'of 12' anchor and does not name the step still open.
problems.fix: Change the early format to: "Step 3 of 12: Need for a Review | Early: Step 2 open (Team's Purpose) | Certified c of 8 | Waiting on you: w | Focus: ..."

problems.problem: Messages 22, 24 and 26 ask Uday to certify the Team's Purpose 'from my last reply' without showing the line again. The persona had to scroll up to find what to approve.
problems.cause: Section 2, point 3 ('Never repeat a table, list ... refer to it in a few words') overrides the pre-send check that 'everything the team must judge is in the reply'.
problems.fix: Add an exception: "Whenever Your turn asks for a certification, show the full CERTIFY line (one line) in that reply, even if it was shown before."

problems.problem: The search reply was very large: a plan map, a field-tag legend, two code blocks with four block tables, a coverage DRAFT, two 10-row review tables, a code-rule table and a not-searched table. Its prose ran to 208 words, over the 180-word cap. The persona said the search strategy was 'buried among many tables' and could not tell which was 'the strategy'.
problems.cause: The prompt caps prose but not tables, requires the plan map at an early start, and allows up to ten rows per table plus every block table.
problems.fix: Add: "In a search reply show three FACT lines, one search card per source, the not-searched table and at most one results table of five rows. Put broader reviews, the selection rule and the plan map behind 'show'; at an early start the status line carries the change, so show the map only on request."

problems.problem: The coverage DRAFT marks fat 'Covered: all 14 name fat'. At least five of the 14 (#9, #10, #12, #13, #14) match only on liver or hepatic fat in NAFLD/MASLD reviews, not on the fat lost with weight, so coverage of the focus is overstated before the need decision.
problems.cause: The agent wrote the selection regex without a kit, and its '\bfat\b' pattern matches any sense of 'fat'. The prompt gives no rule for focus terms with more than one meaning.
problems.fix: Add to Step 3: "Call a focus part covered only when a record reports it as an outcome in the focus's sense; report other senses separately (for example 'names liver fat only: k of 14')." In the kit, provide sense-specific term lists.

problems.problem: Messages 12 and 16 say 'I kept none of your exact words', but the reflection and both CERTIFY lines reproduce Uday's phrase 'what kind of weight is lost, fat or muscle' word for word. The certification reasons are stored as paraphrases Uday never confirmed ('to test the workflow', 'the focus is correct'). The persona said: 'not sure why my words were turned into summaries'.
problems.cause: Prompt 2a ('Without an answer, keep summaries ... do not ask again') and 2b ('write summarized') give no guidance for short phrases or for certification reasons, so the agent added a false disclaimer.
problems.fix: Add: "Without consent, write 'summarized' but never claim that none of the member's words were kept. Keep a certification reason as the reviewer gave it, or ask once at the first CERTIFY line: 'May I keep your words exactly as typed? yes/no'."

problems.problem: Search words for PROSPERO/OSF, Cochrane and Epistemonikos were promised at 22 ('Then I will give you search words') and again at 26 and 28, but had still not been given at the pause (30). The persona could not run those sources, and Step 3 evidence stays incomplete.
problems.cause: Prompt section 2 ('Moving ahead') holds early-step items under Next until the blocking certification. R8 requires strings for sources a member must search, but sets no timing.
problems.fix: Add to the early-start rule: "In the same reply as the automatic searches, give the ready-to-run string for each source a member must search (R8) in a code block, marked 'pending: <member>'."

problems.problem: Asked 'what was the search strategy?', the agent gave a compact table but sent the exact strings to the side file ('Both are also open beside the chat') and offered 'show search 1/2'. The persona's moment 9 requires no file pointer.
problems.cause: Section 2, point 3 ('give its compact form ... and offer show <item>'), combined with the habit of opening a side panel.
problems.fix: Add: "When asked about a search already shown, give the compact table and each exact string in a code block in the chat; do not point to a file."

problems.problem: The When convenient line was repeated at 26 and 30 and grew from e-mail plus model name to three items, adding an unexplained 'OpenAlex access code' (persona: 'I do not know what an access code is for'). Message 14 also mentions 'for the first page of results', which is paging talk when no member had to act.
problems.cause: The prompt lets optional items be listed again at 'what comes next' and at the pause, and does not require saying what each item unlocks when it is first asked.
problems.fix: Add: "Ask each optional item once, with one clause on what it unlocks; list it again only in the pause summary. Mention pages of results only when a member must act."

judge.strengths: Certification integrity was solid. A bare 'Certify' drew only the reason question, 'just start' was not taken as approval, the certified wording matched the shown lines, and the status line never overstated. The early start was announced in one line, did the most useful allowed work, and ended cleanly once the purpose was certified (L000087). The research focus was captured in the persona's own words, reconciled when it narrowed, and carried through the purpose line, the status line and the Step 3 display. The Step 3 search cards were complete: exact strings, per-block counts with sources, the Create-Date bound, records rather than studies, known studies, and the sources not searched with who can run them. The OpenAlex prompt injection asking for the user's e-mail was spotted, ignored and disclosed. The log and per-turn git commits are complete, and counts were rechecked from saved files at the pause. Prose stayed short (median 176 words), with no codes or log ids in sentences. The pause put the summary and plan map in the chat and packaged the workspace only then.
